findings.title: Queued cancellation can be overwritten by concurrent lifecycle writes
findings.scenario: S1 / F1 and strict status-writer variants
findings.summary: The queued-abort handler reads a submitted/dispatched status and acknowledges FINISHED:ABORTED without synchronizing with the runner's earlier status check and subsequent writes. A deployment already past its check can write DISPATCHED over that acknowledgment and later launch the job. The fresh model and controlled implementation trace independently exercise this source-derived F1 mechanism; full local-deployment confirmation remains separate.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 1 (same queued-abort blind status-write mechanism at JC:1058-1080 and JR lifecycle writers)

findings.title: Deleting a listed job can terminate the only scheduling thread
findings.summary: The job manager lists storage objects and later reads each object's metadata without handling concurrent deletion. FilesystemStorage raises when a listed job has disappeared, and JobRunner calls this scan outside its deployment exception handler. The exception escapes the sole scheduling thread, preventing a later eligible job from being considered. This is a source-seeded F2/RS-8 rediscovery; the five-state minimal model path establishes thread death rather than an already-held admission-slot leak.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 2 scan/list/read deletion path (listed job deleted before metadata read kills the scheduler thread)

findings.title: A late RUNNING write can replace an already-published terminal outcome
findings.summary: The runner inserts running_jobs before writing RUNNING to persistent metadata. The completion thread can observe that insertion, classify an already-exited server process and publish a terminal status before the runner resumes its unconditional RUNNING write. The model reproduces the source-derived F3 race with a nonzero early SJ exit; the fresh controlled trace also observes completion removal before the late write. This leaves misleading persisted lifecycle state and still requires independent real-deployment confirmation.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 3 (completion publishes/removes before the runner's late RUNNING write)

findings.title: An early authoritative client failure can make START collection raise KeyError
findings.summary: A client can fail after its process launch succeeds but before all START replies are collected. While the server process entry exists, fail_run records an authoritative failure and removes the pending-outcome entry; START collection later indexes that removed entry directly. The resulting KeyError sends the runner through its generic FAILED_TO_RUN path instead of preserving the authoritative outcome. Both the direct KeyError oracle and outcome oracle reproduce this source-derived F5 mechanism using the real generic-exit remapping rule.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 5 (F5/RS-4 pending client outcome is removed during START collection, leading to KeyError)

findings.title: A metadata refresh can restore SUBMITTED after a successful abort
findings.summary: FilesystemStorage implements a partial metadata update by reading and rewriting the whole metadata dictionary without serializing that read/write interval. A scheduler refresh for a resource-blocked job can capture SUBMITTED, overlap a successful FINISHED:ABORTED update, and then write its old status back. The dedicated F16 probe independently reaches the refresh writer; the generic F16 configuration only finds the shallower F1 deployment race. The fresh controlled trace additionally observes later launch after the lost cancellation.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 13 (scheduler refresh metadata RMW restores SUBMITTED after a successful abort)

findings.title: Competing cleanup paths can terminate the completion thread with KeyError
findings.summary: Completion publishes a terminal status before removing running_jobs, while the startup thread can still be pending at its RUNNING write. A previously authorized deletion makes that late status write raise, and runner exception cleanup removes the same running entry that completion subsequently deletes without a presence check. The unchecked deletion raises KeyError outside a protecting loop handler and kills completion before lifecycle release events. The final C8 38-state counterexample rechecks historical MC-D; it does not constitute a fresh real-code reproduction.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 18 and Scenario 2's MC-D/RS-7 stale-delete cleanup collision (completion blind deletion after runner cleanup)

findings.title: Concurrent process removal can terminate dead-client cleanup
findings.summary: Dead-client notification iterates the live server run_processes dictionary while its body can wait on a child RPC. A process waiter can remove an entry during that wait, causing the iterator's next advance to raise RuntimeError outside the RPC helper's catch. BaseServer.client_cleanup does not catch that exception around remove_dead_clients, so its cleanup thread terminates and later expired clients can remain unprocessed. The model reproduces this source-derived F7 variant; live-client-map and stale-token variants remain separate source-only confirmation candidates.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 6 only for the run-process sweeper live-dictionary iterator; CR-6 retains distinct client-map, stale-token, and admin/shutdown iterator sites

findings.title: Client resources can be freed while same-group descendants remain alive
findings.summary: The client waiter treats leader exit as the point to release the job resources and remove its process registration. Same-process-group descendants can still be alive, while termination either returns after registration disappearance or cannot recover the group through the reaped leader PID. The repaired C8 model witnesses resource release after actual possible SJ/CJ synchronization, leaving the sole unit free while a descendant uses it. This is a source-derived F10 candidate; real local process-group behavior, a supported cooperative subprocess pattern and a later-job allocation control remain mandatory confirmation requirements.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 8 (client resources freed after leader exit while same-group descendants remain alive)

findings.title: Running-job abort can succeed while the final status is COMPLETED
findings.summary: stop_run sends cleanup and abort RPCs before marking the tracked Job as aborted. Completion can observe the resulting clean SJ exit, read the old abort marker, and publish COMPLETED while the handler is still waiting to mark the job. In the final C8 35-state witness, mark_run_aborted then finds the still-tracked Job and returns success without changing that published outcome. This independently rechecks historical MC-E; the earlier C5 witness placed the marker between the abort read and latch. A real abort/RPC/completion schedule and passing nonoverlap control remain separate confirmation obligations.

findings.title: An authoritative client failure recorded after the completion outcome read can be published as success
findings.scenario: S4 / continuation counterexample for the source-review V04 finalization gap
findings.summary: The report handler can pass the pending-outcome check just before completion expires the client-outcome barrier. Completion reads a successful outcome, and fail_run then records an authoritative infrastructure failure while the job is still tracked, but completion latches and publishes its earlier read. This is distinct from an intentionally ignored report after final removal: the implementation accepts and records the active-job failure. The 37-state C8 counterexample refines the source-review V04 concern; actual deadline/handler timing and independent local-deployment reproduction remain required.

findings.title: A client failure accepted in the startup tracking gap can be lost before success is published
findings.summary: The pending-client table becomes active before running_jobs is populated, while an early-exited SJ can already have been removed from run_processes. A failure report can therefore pass the pending check but reach fail_run while neither active map contains the job, causing the failure to be ignored. The runner later inserts the job and completion publishes success without that failure record. The guarded 37-state C8 counterexample independently rechecks historical MC-U1; real supported fast-workflow timing, process failure, deadline/resolution variants and passing active-tracking controls remain confirmation obligations.

findings.title: Stale delete authorization can strand a running job and its admission slot
findings.scenario: S2 / historical MC-C and source stale-delete lead
findings.summary: The delete handler checks the status of an earlier Job snapshot, so a request authorized while SUBMITTED can remove storage after START has succeeded and the job is tracked as RUNNING. When completion later publishes its terminal status, the missing store object makes every retry fail before map removal and lifecycle release. With the concurrency limit occupied, later eligible work cannot be admitted. The fresh 27-state C8 counterexample independently rechecks historical MC-C and excludes the benign interval after successful terminal publication; live completion retry and later-job controls remain confirmation obligations.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 2's MC-C stale delete authorization that strands a running job and admission slot

findings.title: Accepted noncanonical min_clients can repeatedly starve a later eligible job
findings.scenario: S2 / source-seeded F4; pre-reservation numeric-string case
findings.summary: Job validation accepts a numeric string for min_clients by converting it locally, but leaves the original string in persisted metadata, which Job construction retains unchanged. The scheduler then raises TypeError before updating its retry history; its outer catch abandons the whole candidate list. Each later scan retries the same oldest job, so a well-formed later job remains SUBMITTED despite free capacity. The C8 temporal counterexample has five listed states with a loop back to state 1 (seven distinct reachable states) and satisfies the modeled fairness assumptions. This is the original source-seeded F4 mechanism; real public submission, later-job impact and a numeric-value control remain independent confirmation obligations.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 4's pre-reservation numeric-string min_clients case; CR-4 retains distinct null/post-reservation and related malformed-metadata variants

findings.title: Malformed job metadata variants can block later jobs beyond the modeled numeric-string case
findings.summary: MC-13 covers Scenario 4's pre-reservation numeric-string min_clients case, but the brief also calls out null min_clients, nested process-string shapes, and post-reservation failure or expiry accumulation. Those variants hit the same validator-to-scheduler handoff but can differ in whether resources were already reserved before the scheduler exception. Confirmation should use hand-written public job ZIPs and valid-job controls rather than treating the MC-13 counterexample as complete coverage of every malformed-metadata variant.

findings.title: Live dictionary iteration disrupts lifecycle services
findings.summary: MC-7 covers the run-process sweeper iterator, but the source scenario also cites live client-map mutation, stale logout-token handling, stop_all_runs, and training shutdown iteration sites. Those sites use different owners and dictionaries, so the modeled run_processes cardinality race does not represent every mechanism. Confirmation should reproduce each remaining owner/consequence separately, including any admin-command failure or cleanup-thread termination.

findings.title: Fractional GPU accounting fails to restore eligible capacity
findings.summary: GPUResourceManager subtracts and adds requested GPU memory using binary floating-point values, then checks future requests with exact greater-or-equal comparisons. A supported sequence such as reserving and freeing fractional GiB values can leave a restored capacity slightly below the intended amount. This was not represented by the discrete list-unit model, so it remains a code-review candidate for confirmation with a positive-resource configuration and a same-capacity control.

findings.title: Parent death leaves a child in notification retry
findings.summary: The client job process notify_job_status loop retries until a timeout but continues its loop body after logging the timeout, with sleep behavior only in the non-timeout branch. Parent shutdown primarily aborts the local runner, so a child already in this notification path may survive or spin after the parent exits. This parent-death and retry behavior was outside the model, and confirmation must use a real local child process plus a successful-notification control.

findings.title: Disable leaves pending outcomes and slots until the grace expires
findings.summary: ServerEngine.disable_clients removes active client sessions and notifies admin bookkeeping, but the scenario asks whether it skips the normal dead-client outcome resolution path. Job completion waits on pending client outcomes until the configured grace expires when those outcomes are not resolved. No MC finding in the structured list covers this bounded-delay mechanism, so confirmation should distinguish disable, remove, logout, re-enable, and the configured max_jobs/outcome-timeout impact.

findings.title: Overlapping resource consumption changes another job's launch environment
findings.summary: GPUResourceConsumer.consume writes CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES into the client parent process environment before the local launcher copies that environment into a child. If two START handlers overlap, a later allocation can change the parent environment before the first child is spawned. The TLA+ model intentionally did not represent process environment binding, so this remains a code-review candidate requiring a supported overlap and serialization controls.

findings.title: Later empty-resource jobs inherit a stale device binding
findings.summary: A prior positive GPU allocation can leave CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set in the client parent environment. A later job with empty resource requirements may launch without resetting that variable, so it could inherit a stale device view from earlier work. This is distinct from the overlapping-allocation scenario and was not model-checked, so confirmation must establish an operational consequence and a control showing intended zero-GPU visibility.

findings.title: Best-effort SJ status arrival loses an execution error
findings.summary: The server job process reports UPDATE_RUN_STATUS as a best-effort message, while wait_for_complete waits only a short interval before recording and popping process state. If the execution-error update arrives after the pop, fed_server ignores it because the run_processes entry is absent. The current MC findings do not cover this exact best-effort update-loss mechanism, so confirmation must derive the delivery guarantee and use on-time versus delayed-status controls.

findings.title: Ordinary local restart leaves persisted lifecycle state inconsistent
findings.summary: The code has shutdown/restart marker helpers and an update_unfinished_jobs path for RUNNING or DISPATCHED metadata, but the scenario asks whether an ordinary local restart actually reconciles persisted job state with newly empty process tables. The user excluded HA recovery, not every local parent restart, so this source hypothesis remains in scope. No MC candidate in findings.json represents restart semantics, and confirmation must use a real supported restart plus a later-job or status consequence.

findings.title: Cleanup pop races the waiter's return-code observation
findings.summary: ServerEngine.wait_for_complete reads process state, waits briefly for UPDATE_RUN_STATUS, then records and pops the process entry. A concurrent _remove_run_processes path can terminate and pop the same entry, which changes whether the waiter observes the return code or writes through a retained reference. This read/pop/record race is source-only in the consolidated candidate set and must be confirmed with real local process return-code behavior rather than a fabricated PID-reuse premise.

findings.title: Unsafe client failure during startup does not mark the job aborted
findings.summary: An UNSAFE_COMPONENT client failure is routed through stop_run rather than the normal fail_run recording path. stop_run marks a Job aborted only if running_jobs already contains the job, so a startup-window unsafe report can miss that marker. This differs from MC-4 and MC-11 because it depends on the unsafe-code path and stop marker timing, and confirmation must establish a real preserved unsafe return-code path.

findings.title: Empty participants alias the live registered-client dictionary
findings.summary: When start_app_on_server receives an empty job_clients mapping, it substitutes the live client_manager.clients dictionary as the PARTICIPANTS object. Later client registration or removal can mutate that retained object rather than a snapshot. No model-checking candidate covers this aliasing mechanism, so confirmation must establish a supported caller sequence and a concrete iteration, abort, or cleanup consequence.

findings.title: Abort before client registration is dropped before a late start
findings.summary: Client abort handling checks the executor registration state and returns early when a job is still unregistered. The START handler registers a pending handle only later, so a timeout or abort message that arrives before that point may be dropped before a late start proceeds. This is a client-side registration/pending-handle scenario, not the server-side queued-abort mechanism represented by MC-1.

findings.title: Client shutdown and restart lose ownership before child cleanup
findings.summary: Client shutdown and restart create marker files and move the parent toward shutdown while worker process cleanup remains cooperative. If the parent process exits or restarts with empty in-memory ownership state, live child or resource ownership evidence can be lost. This mechanism is not represented by the model, and confirmation must distinguish normal watchdog cleanup from a real survivor that affects later allocation.

findings.title: Re-registration replaces tokens still used by running-job participants
findings.summary: ClientManager can remove an existing token for a client name and issue a new token during re-registration. Running-job PARTICIPANTS can still retain the old token, while heartbeat, dead-job cleanup, and abort targeting consult token-keyed membership. The MC suite only modeled a finite session set and not real token generations, so this scenario remains a source candidate requiring actual same-site re-registration evidence.

findings.title: Typed process failures change meaning across normalization and status mapping
findings.summary: Process-level return codes such as 101, 102, and 103 can be produced by mpm, launcher polling, rc-file reads, and client-side status remapping. Which code survives depends on whether the rc file exists, whether the launcher normalizes it, and whether the client process was STARTING, STARTED, or STOPPED. Current MC findings use modeled categories but do not confirm this end-to-end code path, so confirmation should build an rc-file/control matrix.

findings.title: Fast SJ engine completion is overwritten by STARTED
findings.summary: fed_server.start_run starts the engine thread and then writes MachineStatus.STARTED in the parent thread. The run_engine path can already have completed and written STOPPED before the parent write occurs. This fast server-engine race is separate from the job metadata status overwrites in MC-1 and MC-3, and it needs a real scheduling trigger plus a supported fast controller control.

findings.title: Delayed SJ heartbeat marks normal completion aborted
findings.summary: fed_server treats a server-job heartbeat for a job missing from run_processes as evidence that the job should not be running, then marks the runner Job aborted if persisted metadata still says RUNNING. A delayed heartbeat after process-table removal but before terminal publication could turn normal completion into an abort marker. This late-heartbeat path was not included in the model-checking findings and requires real message-delay and timely-heartbeat controls.

findings.title: Post-spawn setup or cleanup exceptions break resource ownership
findings.summary: ClientExecutor can spawn a local job before starting the waiter thread and before later setup steps complete. If an ordinary post-spawn failure routes through the outer exception path, resources may be freed while a child still lives. Cleanup exceptions after child wait can also skip registry removal, and this ownership/cleanup failure class was outside the converged model except for the specific descendant-lifetime MC-8 candidate.

findings.title: A pending restart or shutdown marker is removed by worker bootstrap
findings.summary: Client worker bootstrap removes restart.fl and shutdown.fl from the site workspace before starting the job process. If an operator or parent control path has placed one of those markers concurrently, bootstrap may consume the command before the intended owner observes it. This lower-priority source scenario is not model-checked, so confirmation must establish the exact marker ownership and a later-job or lifecycle consequence.

findings.title: Partial deployment leaves workspace state relevant to later operations
findings.summary: Deployment can create server or client workspace state before a later target failure causes the job to abort. The _delete_run helper exists, but the scenario notes no demonstrated active failure-path caller for cleaning partial deployment state. No MC candidate covers concrete workspace files or archival cleanup, so confirmation must derive the disk-retention contract and test a later public operation.

findings.title: CAN_NOT_SCHEDULE overwrites an acknowledged abort
findings.summary: The scheduler can publish FINISHED:CAN_NOT_SCHEDULE after updating retry history for blocked jobs. A public abort can write FINISHED:ABORTED before that final scheduler status write, creating a terminal-to-terminal overwrite at a distinct JS:308 site. The final C8 searches did not rediscover this RS-3 scenario, but bounded absence is not coverage, so it remains a code-review candidate.

findings.title: An ordinary cleanup exception escapes completion's narrow catch
findings.summary: The abort-client fanout catches RuntimeError around _send_to_clients but does not catch arbitrary ordinary exceptions from that default path. A non-RuntimeError cleanup exception could escape a lifecycle thread if a concrete default trigger exists. This is not the same as MC-6's unguarded running_jobs deletion, so confirmation should either find an ordinary exception source or classify the case as unsupported.

findings.title: Global machine status differs from concurrent job state
findings.summary: Several paths set the aggregate engine_info.status to STOPPED or STARTED while per-job run_processes may contain different lifecycle facts. A waiter for one server job can set the global status to STOPPED even if another job is still running or starting. This has no MC counterexample in the structured findings, so confirmation must inspect consumers and require a concrete lifecycle or admission consequence rather than a display-only discrepancy.

findings.title: Lock/RPC ordering or late notifications affect cleanup progress
findings.summary: This scenario preserves unresolved source hypotheses around locks held across child RPCs, fail_run and stop_run ordering, and late STARTED/STOPPED notifications. Existing short blocking intervals are not proof of deadlock, but the prompt explicitly says not to drop liveness-only or probably-not-bug candidates. No single MC finding covers this broad set of timing questions, so confirmation must isolate any real cyclic wait, deadline miss, or late-delivery sequence before judging it.

findings.title: Retained SJ status reference can replace a newer failure record
findings.summary: The UPDATE_RUN_STATUS handler can retain a run_process_info reference while wait_for_complete or cleanup later pops the run_processes entry. A subsequent fail_run can create a separate authoritative failure object, and a delayed execution_error UPDATE might assign the retained older object back into exception_run_processes. The current model kept UPDATE atomic and did not establish this reference-lifetime mechanism, so it remains a distinct source-review candidate from MC-10.
